sentences.text: The holotype specimen, the specific fossil used to define the species, includes a skull, lower jaw, and nine neck vertebrae.
Measurements of the neck bones vary, with the first preserved vertebra measuring 16.3 cm in length while the tenth measures 19.9 cm.
The genus name Lishulong means "chestnut tree dragon" and combines the Chinese words for chestnut tree and dragon.
The species name wangi honors Wang Zheng-Ju for his contributions to vertebrate paleontology in the Lufeng region.
The holotype specimen of Lishulong was discovered in 2007 in Jiudu Village, Lufeng County, Yunnan Province, China.
Fragments of the posterior skeleton were found but were lost during the excavation process.
Phylogenetic analysis places Lishulong within the Sauropodiformes as the sister taxon to Yunnanosaurus.
Lishulong lived approximately between 199 and 183 million years ago, spanning the Sinemurian to Toarcian stages, though the time range is also estimated from 199.5 to 174.7 million years ago.
The fossil site of Lishulong is near the discovery location of the theropod dinosaur Panguraptor, suggesting a potential ecological relationship.
